evidence: Compared word by word. SOURCE: 'That’s one grown-up doing three jobs, not three more people moving in to help with the rent, and each job keeps the others in balance.' DRAFT: 'It’s still one grown-up doing three jobs (nobody new is moving in to help with the rent), and each job keeps the others in balance.' The draft matches the_change character for character, and CONTEXT holds it once. KEPT VERBATIM: 'one grown-up doing three jobs', 'moving in to help with the rent' (his rent joke), and the whole tail 'and each job keeps the others in balance'. CHANGED: (1) 'That’s' becomes 'It’s still': the same identity claim (the three named jobs are one grown-up); 'still' only marks the turn from the three capitalised role names just before it (Nurturer, Protector, Guide) to 'this is one person', and adds no fact, condition, person or number. (2) ', not three more people moving in to help with the rent,' becomes '(nobody new is moving in to help with the rent)': the denial of extra people and the rent joke both survive. The one wording delta I weighed is 'three more people' becoming 'nobody new': the count 'three' and 'more' drop out and the denial is marginally more general (no new person at all, rather than not three). I judge that a wording difference, not a claim added or lost: the point (the jobs are not extra people) is identical, and the agent is still the single grown-up. Strength is unchanged (a flat assertion both times). Nothing of his in the line is left out, and the change does not claim to put anything back. His party example, which the SOURCE note says shows the three jobs at work, follows immediately in CONTEXT ('Say a party gets to be too much for your little one...'), and 'It’s you that needs to develop these qualities' still closes the paragraph, so the grown-up is still the reader. READS RIGHT IN CONTEXT: after 'your loving Nurturer, your safe Adult Protector (hereafter just the Protector) and your wise Guide.' the sentence 'It’s still one grown-up doing three jobs (...)' reads naturally; 'It' picks up the arrangement just described (not the inner child, who is not a grown-up), 'still' is earned by the three capitalised roles, and the bracket is in his own manner (he uses '(hereafter just the Protector)' one sentence earlier). TELL ROWS: none PRESENT. Nearest ones I weighed: T16 (his 'That’s X, not Y' reveal is exactly what the change removes; the positive claim now comes first and the denial survives only as his joke in brackets, answering a real misreading of three named roles as three people, which the row itself excludes); T21 (two coordinated clauses plus his bracket joke, the same load as his own line, and the joke is an elaboration of the first clause, not a third job); T26 ('three jobs' repeats the heading and the sentence before it, but the repetition ties the named roles back to one person, as his line did); T12 and T15 (the shape changes and the words are his); T14 (nothing moved or dropped); T17 ('each job keeps the others in balance' is his own clause, kept as written and shown by the party example next); C02 ('It' has a sensible referent); T01, T03, T05, T07, T08, T13, T29 absent (no first person, no new prop, no filler, no image followed by explanation, his joke is noticed inside the line, and it is not the paragraph's last sentence). LINTER: 'D9 follows the source order' is accepted. The change is a one-sentence swap in place, so it follows its source's order by construction, and the paragraph does notice things along the way (the rent joke, the 'still' turn, the party and the bathroom example), so T13 and T09 are not happening. I did not check the Pangram readings quoted in the_change (no web); they are outside this role.
